title: Dogon languages - Wikipedia
text: The Dogon languages are a small closely related language family that is spoken by the Dogon people of Mali and may belong to the proposed Niger–Congo family. There are about 600,000 speakers of its dozen languages.

text: For a long time, the Dogon languages were classified among the Niger-Congo family of languages, but this is now being questioned. Dimmendaal and Heath would rather consider them as an entirely separate family of languages.

title: SONGHAY AND DOGON. : languagehat.com
text: Hausa nama “meat” looks pretty Niger-Congo-ish (cf Kusaal nim “meat”), for example. Mind you, Hausa is a magpie language, like English, forever stealing other people’s words. Even the Hausa word for “two”, biyu, seems not to be Chadic, but borrowed from some Niger-Congo language.
